The marketing evolution

How did business thinking change?

Marketing thinking evolved as markets became more competitive and customers became more informed.
Teacher Tip
These are orientations a business may follow, not strict historical periods. Many firms today still use more than one.

Ask students: Which shop around you still behaves like stage 3?

1

Production concept

🏭 MAKE MORE → SELL MORE

Consumers prefer products that are widely available and affordable.

🏭 Factory📦 Mass production🏷️ Low price🚚 Distribution network
FocusProduction efficiency + availability + affordability
ApproachMass production, low cost, wide distribution
ExampleA company produces thousands of basic products at the lowest possible cost.
Volume ↑ · Cost ↓
Teacher Tip
Link it to the idea of economies of scale: more units, lower cost per unit. Ask where students have seen this mindset (basic packaged goods, early mass-market products).

Mini scenario · Production concept

The Factory Challenge 🏭

A company can produce either:

📦A1,000 units
at ₹500 each
📦📦📦B10,000 units
at ₹250 each

Which strategy represents the Production Concept?

Ask students: What risk does B carry if nobody wants the product?

2

Product concept

⭐ BETTER PRODUCT → MORE CUSTOMERS

Consumers prefer products offering better quality, better performance and better features.

📞Basic Phone
➜
📱Smartphone
➜
💎Premium Smartphone
FocusProduct quality, features and performance
ApproachKeep improving the product again and again
ExampleA smartphone company keeps adding better cameras, faster processors and premium features.
⚠️ Marketing Myopia
A business may focus so much on improving the product that it forgets what customers actually need.
Quality ↑ · Features ↑
Teacher Tip
"Better" is decided by the company here, not by the customer. That gap is exactly where marketing myopia begins.

Spot the mistake

The perfect product… that nobody wants! 😬

A company spends ₹10 crore developing a technically brilliant product. But customers don't buy it.

What went wrong?

The company focused on the product but ignored customer needs.
MARKETING MYOPIA
Short-sighted focus on the product, not on the customer's need.

Ask students: Can you name a "great" product that failed? Why?

3

Selling concept

📢 SELL HARD → SELL MORE

Consumers will not buy enough unless the business uses aggressive selling and promotional efforts.

BUY NOW!LIMITED OFFER!50% OFF📞 Calls📣 Ads
FocusSelling + promotion efforts
ApproachSalespeople, advertisements, discounts, follow-up calls
ExampleInsurance companies and other unsought products use aggressive selling techniques.
Important point
The objective is often to sell what the company has produced, rather than first finding what customers want.
Promotion ↑ · Push ↑
Teacher Tip
Unsought goods (insurance, encyclopaedias) are items buyers don't normally think of buying, so firms push them. Not every sale is bad; the issue is when selling replaces understanding.

Interactive challenge

You are the Sales Manager! 🎯

Your company has 5,000 units of a product left in the warehouse.

What will you do?

Ask students: Choose first, then discuss in pairs.

4

Marketing concept

❤️ CUSTOMER FIRST

Find out what customers want → create it → satisfy them better than competitors.

The turning point of marketing

FocusCustomer needs + satisfaction
ApproachResearch needs, then plan product, price and promotion around them
ExampleA company first understands what customers want, then creates it to satisfy them better than competitors.
Customer at the centre
Teacher Tip
Contrast the direction: Selling goes factory → market. Marketing goes market → factory. Draw both arrows on the board.
🧑‍🤝‍🧑CUSTOMER NEEDS
📊MARKET RESEARCH
📦PRODUCT
🏷️PRICE
📣PROMOTION
😍CUSTOMER SATISFACTION
💰PROFIT
MAKE WHAT YOU CAN SELL, NOT JUST SELL WHAT YOU HAVE MADE.

Teacher Tip
Cover the column headings and read out a cell. Students name the philosophy. Societal Marketing comes next as the "upgrade" of Marketing.
5

Societal marketing concept

🌍 CUSTOMER + COMPANY + SOCIETY

A business should satisfy customer needs while also considering the long-term interests of society.

😊 Customer satisfaction
💰 Company profitability
🤝 Social welfare
🌱 Environmental responsibility
FocusCustomer satisfaction + company profitability + social welfare
ApproachMake ethical, eco-friendly choices in product, packaging and promotion
ExampleA company develops eco-friendly packaging while keeping customers satisfied and staying profitable.
Teacher Tip
It extends the Marketing Concept: customer satisfaction is still needed, but not at the cost of society's long-term well-being.
SUSTAINABLE SUCCESS

Real-life business challenge

Which philosophy would you choose? 🤔

You are launching a new food brand. Which philosophy would create the strongest long-term relationship with customers?

Pick an option to see what it says. 👆
❤️ Marketing Concept + 🌍 Societal Marketing Concept
Understanding customers makes the food brand relevant; caring for health and the environment makes it trustworthy. Satisfied customers and a respected brand give long-term profit and loyalty.
